attempts.raw: TEXT The dot product of two vectors measures how much one vector extends in the direction of the other. Geometrically, it equals the product of their lengths and the cosine of the angle between them. If the vectors are orthogonal (at 90°), their dot product is zero, meaning no projection of one onto the other. A negative dot product indicates an obtuse angle (>90°), showing that the projection of one vector onto the other points opposite to the vector's direction.

attempts.raw: TEXT The dot product of two vectors represents the product of their magnitudes and the cosine of the angle between them. Geometrically, it measures how much one vector projects onto another. When two vectors are orthogonal (at 90°), their dot product is zero, indicating no projection. A negative dot product means the angle between vectors is greater than 90°, so the projection points opposite to the direction of the other vector.
